messages:
Darya: FYI I'm opening a small docs PR to harmonize SOC2 phrasing in the audit export and migration guide. PR link: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4890. Main concerns: wording around pseudonymization, export flags, and retention language.
Kevin: Nice. Can you paste the proposed short blurb for the top of the export section? I want to sanity-check language for platform teams.
Darya: Sure. Draft blurb:
"Audit exports include event-level telemetry for tenant troubleshooting and audits. By default, PII fields (user identifiers, email addresses) are pseudonymized in exported artifacts. Tenants may opt in to include original identifiers; such opt-ins are logged and require documented approval. Retention: default 365 days; events subject to legal hold are retained until released. Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest."
Priya: Legal: prefer replacing "PII" with "personal identifiers" in public docs. Also don't claim irrevocable removal. Suggest: "pseudonymized (irreversible unless tenant enables a mapping export)."
Marco: Agreed. For SOC2 alignment, call out control mapping in a parenthetical e.g., "(SOC2: logging & access controls)" and don't overpromise. Also add a one-line about export auditing: "All export actions are recorded in the tenants audit trail."
Darya: Updated to: "Audit exports include event-level telemetry for tenant troubleshooting and audits. By default, personal identifiers (e.g., email addresses) are pseudonymized in exported artifacts. Tenants can opt in to include original identifiers; opt-ins are recorded in the tenant audit trail and require documented approval. Retention: default 365 days; events under legal hold remain until released. Exports are encrypted in transit and at rest. (See SOC2 mapping.)" Does that address it?
Kevin: Good. Two small tech asks: 1) show examples of the export API flags (pseudonymize vs include_identifiers) with curl and Node snippets, and 2) show a sample CSV row so product folks understand the mapping.
Darya: Adding examples now. Curl example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/export \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"tenant_id":"t_99","since":"2026-01-01","pseudonymize":true}'
```
Node snippet:
```js
// export with pseudonymization
await client.audit.export({ tenantId: 't_99', since: '2026-01-01', pseudonymize: true });
```
CSV sample row shown in docs: `timestamp,tenant,actor,action,tokens,request_id`
`2026-02-20T08:21:00Z,t_99,end_user_pseudonym_0,model.generate,64,req_a1b2`
Priya: Ok but change "pseudonymize: true" explanation: add a parenthetical that mapping is reversible only if tenant requests the mapping export and the tenant key is present. Otherwise pseudonymization is non-reversible by default.
Darya: Done. Also added a tiny section in migration guide explaining how to change existing export scripts from the old flag `redact_personal` to `pseudonymize` and a sample sed command to update repos.
Kevin: Nice touch. Can you include a one-line test snippet for CI that asserts pseudonymized output doesn't contain email regex?
Darya: Yep. Test sample added: `assert not re.search(r"[\w.+-]+@[\w.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}", output_csv)` in the docs test harness.
legal-bot: reminder: include link to Data Retention Policy and Legal Hold runbook.
Darya: Linking both. Also discovered the anchor for `audit-export-guidance` was renamed previously which breaks the export-playbook link; fixing the anchor and adding a redirect.
ci-bot: docs-ci: lint OK; staging preview: https://staging.redwood.ai/docs/audit-export (expires in 48h)
Priya: Last check: change phrase "tenants can opt in" -> "tenants may request inclusion of original identifiers; such requests must be authorized and are recorded." That's clearer for auditors.
Darya: Updated language. Pushed final changes. Please review PR #4890 when you get a sec. I'll request final sign-off from Legal after one more read. Thanks all :sparkles:
